definitionBean.title: Circles and Tangents (Tangent to a Circle)
definitionBean.definition: A line that touches a circle at exactly one point is called a tangent.
definitionBean.explanation: A tangent touches the circle at only one point, called the point of contact. The radius drawn to the point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent, forming an angle of 90°.
importantPoints: A tangent touches a circle at only one point
The radius at the point of contact makes an angle of 90°
Only one tangent can be drawn to a circle from a point on it
Tangents and radii are perpendicular to each other

definitionBean.title: Properties of Tangents (Properties of Tangents)
definitionBean.definition: The lengths of the two tangents drawn to a circle from an external point are always equal.
definitionBean.explanation: If two tangents PA and PB are drawn to a circle from an external point P, then PA = PB. Also, the line joining the center O to P bisects angle APB.
importantPoints: The lengths of both tangents drawn from an external point are equal (PA = PB)
The line joining the center to the external point bisects the angle
The tangent is perpendicular to the radius

parts.statement: From a point Q, the length of the tangent to a circle is 24 cm and the distance of Q from the center is 25 cm. Find the radius of the circle.
parts.explanation:
Given:
Tangent length (PQ) = 24 cm
Distance of the point from the center (OQ) = 25 cm

We know that the radius of a circle is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact.
Therefore, triangle OPQ is a right-angled triangle, in which ∠OPQ = 90°.

From the Pythagorean theorem:
OQ² = OP² + PQ²
(25)² = OP² + (24)²
625 = OP² + 576
OP² = 625 - 576
OP² = 49
OP = 7 cm

Therefore, the radius of the circle is 7 cm.

parts.statement: If TP and TQ are two tangents to a circle with center O such that ∠POQ = 110°, then find ∠PTQ.
parts.explanation:
Given:
∠POQ = 110°

In quadrilateral OPTQ (where P and Q are points of contact):
The radii OP and OQ are perpendicular to the tangents TP and TQ respectively.
Therefore, ∠OPT = 90° and ∠OQT = 90°.

The sum of all angles in a quadrilateral is 360°:
∠PTQ + ∠OPT + ∠OQT + ∠POQ = 360°
∠PTQ + 90° + 90° + 110° = 360°
∠PTQ + 290° = 360°
∠PTQ = 360° - 290°
∠PTQ = 70°

parts.statement: A tangent PQ at a point P of a circle of radius 5 cm meets a line through the center O at a point Q so that OQ = 12 cm. Find the length of PQ.
parts.explanation:
Given:
Radius (OP) = 5 cm
Distance from the center (OQ) = 12 cm

The tangent is perpendicular to the radius, therefore ∠OPQ = 90°.
In right-angled triangle OPQ, using the Pythagorean theorem:
OQ² = OP² + PQ²
(12)² = (5)² + PQ²
144 = 25 + PQ²
PQ² = 144 - 25
PQ² = 119
PQ = √119 cm

Therefore, the length of PQ is √119 cm.

parts.statement: If PA and PB are two tangents from an external point P to a circle with center O such that ∠APB = 80°, then find ∠POA.
parts.explanation:
We know that the line joining the center to the external point bisects the angle between the tangents.
Therefore, ∠APO = (1/2) × ∠APB = (1/2) × 80° = 40°.

The tangent is perpendicular to the radius, therefore ∠OAP = 90°.
In right-angled triangle OAP:
∠POA + ∠APO + ∠OAP = 180°
∠POA + 40° + 90° = 180°
∠POA + 130° = 180°
∠POA = 180° - 130° = 50°
